**Footnotes/ references**

[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-10-K-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-2)

**Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.** is an American multinational [entertainment company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_industry "Entertainment industry") that was founded in 2010 following the [merger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mergers_and_acquisitions "Mergers and acquisitions") of [Live Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_(events_promoter) "Live Nation (events promoter)") and [Ticketmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticketmaster "Ticketmaster"). It continues to operate both brands as subsidiary companies, promoting and managing ticket sales for live entertainment internationally. It also owns and operates entertainment venues and manages the careers of music artists.

The company has faced widespread criticism over its central role in the [consolidation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidation_(business) "Consolidation (business)") of the live events industry, allegations that it proactively engages in [anti-competitive practices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-competitive_practices "Anti-competitive practices"), poor handling of the ticket sale process for highly popular events, and injuries and deaths that have occurred at many of its events.

As of early 2023, Live Nation's annual shareholders report says the company has controlling interests in 338 venues globally and believes itself to be "the largest live entertainment company in the world," "the largest producer of live music concerts in the world," "the world’s leading live entertainment ticketing sales and marketing company," and "one of" the world's biggest artist management companies and music advertising networks for corporate brands.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-2022_Annual_Report-3)

In May 2024, the Justice Department and a coalition of states [sued to break up Live Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_v._Live_Nation_Entertainment "United States v. Live Nation Entertainment") over antitrust violations.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-4)

In 2009, [Live Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_(events_promoter) "Live Nation (events promoter)") and [Ticketmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticketmaster "Ticketmaster"), a concert promotion firm and ticketing company, reached an agreement to merge. The new company received regulatory approval and was named Live Nation Entertainment.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-6)[Michael Rapino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Rapino "Michael Rapino"), then CEO of Live Nation, became the new company's CEO, while Ticketmaster CEO [Irving Azoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Azoff "Irving Azoff") was named executive chairman.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-7)

The merger was approved first in Norway and Turkey in 2009.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:0-8) The United Kingdom's [Competition Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Competition_Commission "Competition Commission") provisionally ruled against the merger,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-9) but reversed its decision on December 22, 2009.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:0-8)

The merger was opposed in the U.S. by some regulators, artists, fans, and competing firms, who argued it would reduce competition in the industry and increase ticket costs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-11)[Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") musician [Bruce Springsteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen") was a vocal opponent of the merger at the time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-12)

On January 25, 2010, the [U.S. Justice Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Justice_Department "United States Justice Department") approved the merger pending certain conditions.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-Chmielewski-13) Ticketmaster had to sell ownership of its self-ticketing company, [Paciolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paciolan "Paciolan"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-Chmielewski-13) and license its software to [Anschutz Entertainment Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anschutz_Entertainment_Group "Anschutz Entertainment Group") (AEG), which would allow it to compete "head-to-head" with Ticketmaster for business.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:1-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:3-15) AEG was given the option after five years to buy the software, replace it with something else, or partner with another ticketing company.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:1-14) Additionally, Live Nation Entertainment was placed under a 10-year court order prohibiting it from retaliating against venues that choose to accept competing ticket contracts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:3-15)

Investments and growth
----------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Investments and growth")]

In 2017, Live Nation Entertainment reported revenue of $10.3 billion.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:4-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-17)

In April 2018, the [United States Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice") launched an investigation following allegations by AEG that Live Nation pressured them into using Ticketmaster and intentionally avoided booking acts for AEG venues.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:2-18) Live Nation stated that decisions in selecting venues were not punitive, and were instead based on size and management.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:2-18)

In 2020, Live Nation was hit particularly hard by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), with essentially all concerts and sporting events around the world on hold. The company has been sued as it has been reluctant to offer full refunds to customers,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-19) though it has since amended its refund rules to address those complaints. On February 25, 2021, Live Nation released its full-year 2020 financial results, of which the company saw revenues fall by 84%.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-20)

### Northeastern United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Northeastern United States")]

In 2016, Live Nation acquired Founders Entertainment, the [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City")-based parent company of the [Governors Ball Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Ball_Music_Festival "Governors Ball Music Festival").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-21) In 2017, Live Nation announced New York City-based promotion company Mercury East in partnership with Michael Swier, a founder of [The Bowery Presents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bowery_Presents "The Bowery Presents"), since acquired by [AEG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anschutz_Entertainment_Group "Anschutz Entertainment Group").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-2017_NYT-22) The deal brought former "indie" clubs [Mercury Lounge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Lounge "Mercury Lounge") and [Bowery Ballroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowery_Ballroom "Bowery Ballroom") under the Live Nation umbrella,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-2017_NYT-22) along with other Live Nation-owned venues including [Irving Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Plaza "Irving Plaza"), [Gramercy Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramercy_Theatre "Gramercy Theatre"), and the [Ford Amphitheater at Coney Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Amphitheater_at_Coney_Island "Ford Amphitheater at Coney Island").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-23)

In 2021, Live Nation announced a joint venture with Duke Concept, a concert promoter specialising in African artists, in which Duke Concept handles production and logistics with Live Nation providing support and a network of venues, for touring [Afrobeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrobeat "Afrobeat") artists.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-24)

### Western United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Western United States")]

In 2013, Live Nation announced a joint venture with [Insomniac Events](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insomniac_Events "Insomniac Events"), a promoter focused on [electronic dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-26) The company continued to invest in music festivals and promoters in 2017, purchasing a controlling interest in [BottleRock Napa Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BottleRock_Napa_Valley "BottleRock Napa Valley") Music Festival,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-27) Salt Lake City-based concert promoter United Concerts,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-28) and CT Touring.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-29)

In 2021, Live Nation acquired a majority stake in streaming entertainment company Veeps.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-30)

### Southern United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Southern United States")]

In 2013, the company acquired the New Orleans [Voodoo Music + Arts Experience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voodoo_Music_%2B_Arts_Experience "Voodoo Music + Arts Experience").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-31) Live Nation later acquired [C3 Presents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C3_Presents "C3 Presents") in [Austin, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas "Austin, Texas") (2014),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-32) Bonnaroo Music and Arts Festival in Tennessee (2015),[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-33) Knoxville-based AC Entertainment (2016),[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-34) Red Mountain Entertainment (2018),[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-35) and Emporium Presents.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-36)

In October 2019, Live Nation acquired a majority stake in [David Grutman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Grutman "David Grutman")'s Groot Hospitality, which includes several nightclubs and restaurants in the [Miami metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_metropolitan_area "Miami metropolitan area"), including the [Fontainebleau Miami Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fontainebleau_Miami_Beach "Fontainebleau Miami Beach") hotel's [LIV nightclub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LIV_(nightclub) "LIV (nightclub)").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-37)

### Midwestern United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Midwestern United States")]

In 2018, the company acquired majority stakes in [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin")-based Frank Productions.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-38)

In August 2015, Live Nation announced it would form Live Nation Germany, in partnership with [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germans "Germans") promoter [Marek Lieberberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marek_Lieberberg "Marek Lieberberg"). Live Nation Germany would also have oversight over Live Nation events in [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria") and [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-39) In 2017, the company purchased a controlling stake in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom")-based Cuffe & Taylor.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:5-40) The company expanded into [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal "Portugal") in 2024, acquiring the [MEO Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MEO_Arena "MEO Arena") in [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-41) In December 2025, it was announced Live Nation Entertainment was to acquire [Royal Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Arena "Royal Arena"), a multi-use indoor arena in [Copenhagen, Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copenhagen,_Denmark "Copenhagen, Denmark") for an undisclosed amount.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-42)

In 2017, Live Nation purchased a controlling interest in [Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel") promoter Blue Stone Entertainment.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:5-40)

In April 2020, it was disclosed that [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia")'s [Public Investment Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Investment_Fund "Public Investment Fund") (PIF) recently acquired a 5.7% stake in Live Nation, as of April 28, 2020, the investment was valued at just shy of $500 million. The transaction, performed on the open market, made the PIF Live Nation's third-largest shareholder.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-44)

On April 25, 2022, Live Nation acquired [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines")-based promoter Music Management International (MMI) to create its local branch.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-45) Filipina businesswoman Rhiza Pascua, who founded MMI in 1996, became managing director of Live Nation Philippines following the acquisition.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-46)

In February 2016, Live Nation acquired Canada's largest independent concert promoter, Union Events.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-47)

In May 2018, Live Nation Entertainment also acquired a majority stake in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil")'s [Rock in Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_in_Rio "Rock in Rio") festival, including from previous stakeholder [SFX Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SFX_Entertainment "SFX Entertainment"), which was involved in a failed attempt at a [U.S. version of the event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_in_Rio_USA "Rock in Rio USA") in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), with its founder Roberto Medina continuing to manage the festival's operations, and providing consulting to Live Nation.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-auto-48)

In March 2016, Live Nation acquired Big Concerts International, South Africa's leading concert promoter.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-49)

Operating divisions
-------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Operating divisions")]

Live Nation Entertainment's business segments are concerts, ticketing, and sponsorship and advertising.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:4-16) The company promotes and operates live music events and manages artists under its concerts division [Live Nation Concerts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_(events_promoter) "Live Nation (events promoter)").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:4-16) Live Nation Entertainment's artist management arm, called Artist Nation, is included within its concerts division[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-50)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:4-16) and also includes Front Line Management and [Roc Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roc_Nation "Roc Nation").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-51) Live Nation Entertainment owns and operates hundreds of venues globally.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-2022_Annual_Report-3) The company sells tickets to live events through [Ticketmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticketmaster "Ticketmaster").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:4-16)

The company has faced various lawsuits alleging ticket [price fixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_fixing "Price fixing"), hidden fees and [anti-competitive practices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-competitive_practices "Anti-competitive practices").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-54)

[Destiny's Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny%27s_Child "Destiny's Child") manager [Mathew Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Knowles "Mathew Knowles") unsuccessfully sued Live Nation in 2011, asserting that the company had spread false information about his business dealings with [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-55)

In May 2022, [Representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") for [New Jersey's 9th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey%27s_9th_congressional_district "New Jersey's 9th congressional district")[Bill Pascrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Pascrell "Bill Pascrell") stated that he had issued letters to the [Federal Trade Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Trade_Commission "Federal Trade Commission") and [U.S. Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Department_of_Justice "U.S. Department of Justice") calling for Live Nation to be unwound and broken up, citing its safety record and other factors.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-56) These calls were repeated in November 2022 after the Taylor Swift ([The Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour")) [Ticketmaster controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Ticketmaster_controversy "2022 Ticketmaster controversy").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-57)

On August 2, 2023, Dynamic Ticket Systems, LLC. sued [Ticketmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticketmaster "Ticketmaster") and Live Nation for patent infringement.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-59)

In May 2024,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-60) the company confirmed rumours of a 1.3 TB[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-61) data leak,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-62) at subsidiary Ticketmaster,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-63) whose potential impact may extend to over 500 million of their customers,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-64) making it one of the world's biggest digital security breaches.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-65) The leak was attributed to the malicious efforts of [ShinyHunters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ShinyHunters "ShinyHunters"), a hacker group who allegedly targeted the company's [Snowflake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowflake_Inc. "Snowflake Inc.") (cloud-based)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-66) infrastructure.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-67) The incident led to a class action lawsuit.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-69)

In August of 2024, Ireland’s consumer watchdog ruled out an investigation into ticket pricing "after some tickets jumped in price by over 400 per cent on Ticketmaster within minutes"[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-70) and failures of their website[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-71) during sales of upcoming concerts for the band [Oasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oasis_(band) "Oasis (band)") to be performed in August 2025.

In September 2025, the [Federal Trade Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Trade_Commission "Federal Trade Commission") in the United States and seven US states sued [Ticketmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticketmaster "Ticketmaster") and Live Nation, alleging the company engaged in illegal resale tactics that cost consumers billions of dollars. The lawsuit claims the companies colluded with brokers to collect tickets and then sell them at higher prices, and that advertised limits on broker sales on the Ticketmaster platform were not enforced.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-72)

### Department of Justice lawsuit

On May 23, 2024, the [U.S. Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Department_of_Justice "U.S. Department of Justice") announced it was [suing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_v._Live_Nation_Entertainment "United States v. ### Injuries and deaths

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Injuries and deaths")]

Live Nation has been linked to at least 200 deaths and 750 injuries at its events in seven countries since 2006. From 2016 to 2019, they had also been cited for at least ten [OSHA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupational_Safety_and_Health_Act_(United_States) "Occupational Safety and Health Act (United States)") violations, fined for several more serious incidents, and [sued civilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_lawsuit "Civil lawsuit") at least once for a concert incident.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-auto2-75)

In June 2013, Live Nation was charged with violating [Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario "Ontario") health and safety laws following [a 2012 stage collapse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiohead_stage_collapse "Radiohead stage collapse") at a [Radiohead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiohead "Radiohead") concert that killed one crew member.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-Technician_death-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-77) A 2019 inquest returned a verdict of [accidental death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accidental_death "Accidental death").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-78) A British inquest later that year found that inadequate technical advice and construction techniques had caused the death.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-79)

On October 1, 2017, the [Route 91 Harvest Festival shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Las_Vegas_shooting "2017 Las Vegas shooting") left 58 people dead and hundreds more injured. It is the [deadliest mass shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_shootings_in_the_United_States "Mass shootings in the United States") in US history. The shooter fired at attendees from the 32nd floor of [Mandalay Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandalay_Bay "Mandalay Bay").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-80) The victims settled for $800 million and received their settlements four years after the shooting.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-81)

In November 2021, a [crowd crushing incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astroworld_Festival_crowd_crush "Astroworld Festival crowd crush") occurred at [Astroworld Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astroworld_Festival "Astroworld Festival")—a Live Nation-promoted concert in Houston organized and headlined by rapper [Travis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Scott "Travis Scott")—which resulted in 10 fatalities[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-83) and nearly 5,000 injuries.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-84) Live Nation, Scott, and other parties involved have been named in over 387 lawsuits related to the incident, which in January 2022 were combined down into a single case.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-Fourcategories-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-87) In December 2021, the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress")[House Oversight Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Oversight_and_Reform "United States House Committee on Oversight and Reform") announced a bipartisan investigation into Live Nation's role in the incident.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-89)

In February 2022, the family of [Drakeo the Ruler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drakeo_the_Ruler "Drakeo the Ruler") filed a [wrongful death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrongful_death_claim "Wrongful death claim") lawsuit against Live Nation in the [Los Angeles County Superior Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Superior_Court "Los Angeles County Superior Court"), after the rapper was killed in a [homicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homicide "Homicide") that occurred backstage at the Once Upon a Time in LA music festival at [BMO Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMO_Stadium "BMO Stadium"). The suit claimed that Live Nation had negligently failed to employ proper and effective security measures at the event. Live Nation sought a [motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_(legal) "Motion (legal)") to dismiss the suit, arguing that the incident was rare and "unforeseen". In January 2023, judge Yolanda Orozc rejected the motion and allowed the suit to continue, ruling that "the fact that defendants knew security would be needed for the event, supports the finding that the performing artists’ safety was a concern for defendants and foreseeable to defendants."[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-92)

### Bellwether Arbitration and New Era ADR

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Live_Nation_Entertainment&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Bellwether Arbitration and New Era ADR")]

An antitrust [class action lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_action "Class action") filed by four customers of Ticketmaster in 2023 alleged that two years earlier, when Live Nation was about to be faced with large amounts of demands for arbitration, that the company changed its arbitration provider and rules from [JAMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAMS_(organization) "JAMS (organization)") to a startup, New Era ADR, who had rules and procedures much friendlier to Live Nation. In _Skot Heckman et al v. Live Nation_, an antitrust case based on Live Nation's inflated ticket prices, the initial filings described New Era's rules and procedures as abusive and "[Kafkaesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Kafka "Franz Kafka")", and Live Nation's switch from JAMS to New Era as unfair since they made the decision to switch arbitration providers unilaterally and without sufficient notice. A prior filing also alleged that Live Nation had a hand in writing New Era's rules. Live Nation's switch to New Era and its rules were primarily based on its friendlier terms to Live Nation and its requirement that in instances where multiple related cases were filed into a "bellwether" arbitration system, where three cases would be decided in an expedited fashion and if settlements could not be reached after the three cases were decided, that the result of the three cases would apply to the rest of the cases automatically. New Era's rules further included limiting filings to ten pages, briefs to five pages, prohibitions on [Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_(law) "Discovery (law)"), and a maximum of 10 documents as evidence, which the plaintiffs described as “absurd” and which would severely hinder the probability impossible for bellwether claimants to meet antitrust pleading standards in their individual cases – let alone to protect the interests of all of the other claimants, current and future, whom would be bound by rulings from the bellwether proceedings.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:6-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-94)

Live Nation counter argued that New Era's rules were valid and that a simple rule change should not prohibit the arbitration clause from being enforced, and that the bellwether procedures should be used in order so that claims get decided quickly; Live Nation's attorneys further alleged that plaintiffs only sued over the arbitration rules in order to gain “outsized settlement leverage” with Live Nation, citing the large fees that would have been charged to Live Nation if JAMS were to stay as arbitrator.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-:6-93)

Ultimately, federal judge [George H. Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._Wu "George H. Wu"), who was overseeing the proposed class action, ruled that the changing of arbitrators unilaterally made the entire arbitration agreement unconscionable, and kept in place the ability for class action status to be certified. Wu found in August 2023 that Live Nation's rule changes to potentially be "fundamentally unfair", and that New Era had "unchecked power" to group cases together as part of the bellwether arbitration process, and that New Era's limits could not reasonably allow plaintiffs to prove their case. Furthermore, Wu found that Live Nation offerings were often the only places in certain regions to find events, and that patrons were effectively forced into either accepting Live Nation's terms or forgoing attending live events altogether.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-95) On appeal to the [Ninth Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Ninth_Circuit "United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit"), the court concurred with Wu, with judges calling New Era's rules "cockamamie" and "just nuts".[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment#cite_note-98)

LIV Nightclub in Las Vegas, located at the iconic Fontainebleau Las Vegas, is set to redefine the city’s nightlife experience. This 50,000 square-foot venue, a much-anticipated expansion of the celebrated LIV Nightclub from Miami, promises high-energy, A-list entertainment in a luxurious setting. The club features 62 VIP tables strategically built around its DJ booth, ensuring that all 2,000 guests feel immersed in the action and have a clear view of the DJ. LIV’s DJ lineup for 2024 is expected to include big names like John Summit, Tiesto, and Zedd, and will host a special Hip-Hop night every Sunday.

LIV Nightclub operates from Friday through Sunday nights, from 10:00 pm to 4:00 am, with average wait times around 1 hour. General admission starts at $30 for women and $50 for men, with VIP bottle service starting at $2000. The club enforces a strict dress code, requiring collared shirts for men and fashion-forward attire for women. The club’s design includes state-of-the-art technology, sound, and a video wall with dual-sided LED screens, ensuring an unparalleled nightclub experience.

With its roots in the vibrant nightlife of Miami, LIV Las Vegas is poised to become a premier destination for celebrities, music enthusiasts, and party-goers seeking an unforgettable night in the heart of Las Vegas.

Ayrton Lighting Fixtures and grandMA3 Control Love the Nightlife at LIV Las Vegas
=================================================================================

With its expansion to the famed Strip, Fontainebleau Las Vegas has launched LIV Las Vegas, the city’s newest nightlife destination, which Lighting Designer Stephen Lieberman has illuminated with an array of Ayrton fixtures controlled by a grandMA3 light console. ACT Entertainment is the exclusive distributor of Ayrton and MA Lighting products in North America.

Fontainebleau Las Vegas brings a new era of luxury hospitality to the Strip and promises a night like no other at its LIV Las Vegas nightclub. The LIV brand from Groot Hospitality was born at the iconic Fontainebleau Miami in 2008. Now, its 50,000 square-foot counterpart in Las Vegas delivers high-energy, A-list entertainment to that city’s clubgoers making its 2,000 guests feel in the middle of the EDM action.

Lieberman, who is President of LA-area SJ Lighting, which specializes in production systems for nightlife and hospitality, already had designed the lighting for LIV Miami when his firm was hired to design and develop the theatrical system for LIV Las Vegas. His team worked in collaboration with BWA Architects, Rockwell Group interior designers and Sound Investment AV audio designers.

“One of the challenges was having all the designers come together from different cities and make everything look coordinated – that’s as daunting a task as the actual design work,” Lieberman explains. “The theatrical lighting needed to include hybrid fixtures, wash lights to balance the look, strobes, LED strip lights, lasers and LED video panels with a high level of automation.

“The space is very fluid with a very clean layout and great sight lines: You’re able to do a lap around the first floor and second-level mezzanine and not get stuck in a dead end,” he says. “Whether you are at a table or a bar, you’re an active participant in the show, and we did our best to make the experience as immersive as possible.”

The interior has soft, curved radial lines with an hourglass-shaped ceiling feature composed of two connected ellipses that move up and down. Another ellipse encloses six-part LED video panels, which also move up and down. “There’s a lot of motion over the dance floor for a very animated environment,” Lieberman notes. Tables surround the dance floor and the mezzanine with bars left and right. The central DJ booth has enough counter space in front to serve as a performance stage, while coveted VIP tables are inside the booth.

Having had “good success with Ayrton Diablos in the past” Lieberman decided to use them at LIV Las Vegas. “We love their clean optics and nice aesthetic, and they have the right feature set,” he reports. Forty-four Diablos do the heavy lifting throughout the space providing clean, even coverage from positions in the automated ellipses and under the mezzanine where they create layers of light.

The Diablos are supported by 48 Ayrton MagicDot SX luminaires. “We wanted to stay with the same manufacturer for the moving lights for ease of coordination,” says Lieberman. “The MagicDots are compact, bright washes with zoom capabilities. Their 360º pan and tilt is an added feature for the rig.”

Six Ayrton Levantes are mounted near the stage for special looks and key lighting for the DJs and performers. “The Levantes were new to us, but when you build spaces like this having the right equipment for specials is critical. Sometimes you have to allocate fixtures that are already part of the show. But here we didn’t have to sacrifice part of the big rig to light other positions. The Levantes have enough firepower, even when they’re throttled back, to cut through video and other lighting. They do exactly what we need them to do.”

He notes that his company’s close relationship with ACT Entertainment was a big factor in his use of Ayrton fixtures for LIV Las Vegas. “It’s important to us to not only choose quality equipment but also to have people who stand behind it supporting the gear. Having ACT behind the Ayrton line meant a lot to us.”

A grandMA3 light console controls lighting from a position in the DJ booth. It is interconnected with the video and automation control systems.

“I’ve been using grandMA since the original version back in 2001, and we’re running grandMA3 in clubs now,” Lieberman reports. “The light’s smaller footprint is key where space is at a premium. We programmed the system and trained the staff. We like to think we have a good philosophy of how to lay out the console intuitively in terms of what’s important to the operator. Within 48 hours the in-house operators felt very comfortable with the system.”

“Everything is performing fantastically,” he says. “The support we got from ACT was paramount to the success of the venue.”

We and [our 991 partners](https://issuu.com/mondiale/docs/md34-4_digital_issuu/102#) process your personal data, e.g. your IP-number, using technology such as cookies to store and access information on your device in order to serve personalized ads and content, ad and content measurement, audience research and services development. You have a choice in who uses your data and for what purposes. Your privacy choices are only applicable on this digital property where you have made your choices. You can change or withdraw your consent any time from the Cookie Declaration or by clicking on the Privacy trigger icon.

If you allow, we would also like to: 
*   Collect information about your geographical location which can be accurate to within several meters
*   Identify your device by actively scanning it for specific characteristics (fingerprinting)

Find out more about how your personal data is processed and set your preferences in the [details section](https://issuu.com/mondiale/docs/md34-4_digital_issuu/102#).

When we use the word “cookies”, we mean any tracking technology that stores or accesses information on the user’s device, including any SDK, tracking pixel, HTML5 local storage, local shared object, and fingerprinting technique.

- [x] Store and/or access information on a device 

Cookies, device or similar online identifiers (e.g. login-based identifiers, randomly assigned identifiers, network based identifiers) together with other information (e.g. browser type and information, language, screen size, supported technologies etc.) can be stored or read on your device to recognise it each time it connects to an app or to a website, for one or several of the purposes presented here.
Examples:*   Most purposes explained in this notice rely on the storage or accessing of information from your device when you use an app or visit a website. For example, a vendor or publisher might need to store a cookie on your device during your first visit on a website, to be able to recognise your device during your next visits (by accessing this cookie each time).

- [x] Use limited data to select advertising 

- [x] Legitimate Interest 

Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times an ad is presented to you).
Examples:*   A car manufacturer wants to promote its electric vehicles to environmentally conscious users living in the city after office hours. The advertising is presented on a page with related content (such as an article on climate change actions) after 6:30 p.m. to users whose non-precise location suggests that they are in an urban zone.
*   A large producer of watercolour paints wants to carry out an online advertising campaign for its latest watercolour range, diversifying its audience to reach as many amateur and professional artists as possible and avoiding showing the ad next to mismatched content (for instance, articles about how to paint your house). The number of times that the ad has been presented to you is detected and limited, to avoid presenting it too often.

- [x] Create profiles for personalised advertising 

Information about your activity on this service (such as forms you submit, content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (for example, information from your previous activity on this service and other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (that might include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present advertising that appears more relevant based on your possible interests by this and other entities.
Examples:*   If you read several articles about the best bike accessories to buy, this information could be used to create a profile about your interest in bike accessories. Such a profile may be used or improved later on, on the same or a different website or app to present you with advertising for a particular bike accessory brand. If you also look at a configurator for a vehicle on a luxury car manufacturer website, this information could be combined with your interest in bikes to refine your profile and make an assumption that you are interested in luxury cycling gear.
*   An apparel company wishes to promote its new line of high-end baby clothes. It gets in touch with an agency that has a network of clients with high income customers (such as high-end supermarkets) and asks the agency to create profiles of young parents or couples who can be assumed to be wealthy and to have a new child, so that these can later be used to present advertising within partner apps based on those profiles.

Special Purposes 3

Ensure security, prevent and detect fraud, and fix errors 

Your data can be used to monitor for and prevent unusual and possibly fraudulent activity (for example, regarding advertising, ad clicks by bots), and ensure systems and processes work properly and securely. It can also be used to correct any problems you, the publisher or the advertiser may encounter in the delivery of content and ads and in your interaction with them.
Examples:*   An advertising intermediary delivers ads from various advertisers to its network of partnering websites. It notices a large increase in clicks on ads relating to one advertiser, and uses data regarding the source of the clicks to determine that 80% of the clicks come from bots rather than humans.

Deliver and present advertising and content 

Certain information (like an IP address or device capabilities) is used to ensure the technical compatibility of the content or advertising, and to facilitate the transmission of the content or ad to your device.
Examples:*   Clicking on a link in an article might normally send you to another page or part of the article. To achieve this, 1°) your browser sends a request to a server linked to the website, 2°) the server answers back (“here is the article you asked for”), using technical information automatically included in the request sent by your device, to properly display the information / images that are part of the article you asked for. Technically, such exchange of information is necessary to deliver the content that appears on your screen.

MONDO-DR is the international publication for technology in entertainment. Established in 1990, the magazine has held a presence in the international marketplace for over 30 years, covering some of the most impressive installations from around the world, including; theatres, nightclubs, theme parks, and houses of worship, to name but a few. Targeted at venues, distributors, dealers, installers and system integrators, MONDO-DR provides unrivalled, in-depth editorial, read by the major decision makers and buyers worldwide. MONDO-DR constantly works to build on its distribution through a commitment to exhibiting or visiting most international tradeshows and visiting emerging markets. MONDO-DR is also the organiser of the MONDO-DR Awards, launched in 2017 – the only awards event dedicated to recognising and celebrating entertainment installations.

### Time Out says

LIV has been leading the pack in Miami’s club scene since it debuted in 2008 as the crown jewel of the Fontainebleau Hotel’s unprecedented billion-dollar renovation. With top-tier talent (Skrillex and Bieber once performed in the same weekend) and insane six-figure bottle service (Mark Cuban allegedly dropped more than 100 grand on a single bottle of champagne in 2013), LIV quickly showed the nightlife world that Miami’s best days are not in the past. “Our grand opening was for the Victoria’s Secret fashion show and, each night since, we’ve continued to change production and create a new party on a nightly basis,” says owner David Grutman.

But even the giants must learn to adapt. And one of LIV’s biggest challenges came last summer as the club closed for months to undergo a $10 million renovation. “We’ll never stay complacent,” says Grutman, referring to the overhaul that added more than 400 digitally controlled LED panels to create choreographed light shows that take up the club’s entire domed ceiling. On its sneak-peek weekend—in typical star-studded fashion—Travis Scott, Skrillex and Lil Wayne performed on the brand-new stage. “The new look gives fans more of a 360-degree experience, and you’ll know what I mean once you’ve experienced it,” says Grutman, hinting at a shift in programming. “The world changes on a constant basis, and so does music. Fridays will remain open format, Saturday we’ll have dance music and LIV On Sunday remains the biggest hip-hop party in the world, but we have new surprises on Wednesday and Thursday that will launch in the next couple months.”

![Image 1](https://www.edmtunes.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Fontainebleau-Las-Vegas-Opening-696x392.jpeg)

_\*Featured Cover Photo Credit: Fontainebleau Las Vegas_

After it broke ground in 2007, the **Fontainebleau Las Vegas** hotel and resort will finally open **December 13, 2023**. According to [an article](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lifestyle/lifestyle-news/fontainebleau-las-vegas-opening-date-liv-nightclub-1235592531/) from _The Hollywood Reporter_, [the new resort](https://www.fontainebleaulasvegas.com/) will also open up the latest franchise of the prestigious **[LIV Nightclub](https://www.edmtunes.com/2017/06/miamis-liv-plans-10-million-renovation/)**, as well as **LIV Beach**, on the same day. Fontainebleau Las Vegas, which is also the sister hotel to the **Fontainebleau Miami Beach** that the famous ‘Rat Pack’ used to frequent, broke ground under the leadership of **Jeff Soffer**. He is the CEO and chairman of Fontainebleau Las Vegas and he acquired the resort and hotel’s property in 2000.

[![Image 2](https://www.edmtunes.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/LIV-Beach_Courtesy-of-Rockwell-Group.webp)](https://www.edmtunes.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/LIV-Beach_Courtesy-of-Rockwell-Group.webp)

[![Image 3](https://www.edmtunes.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/LIV-Fontainebleau-Las-Vegas-Publicity-H-2023-1024x577.webp)](https://www.edmtunes.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/LIV-Fontainebleau-Las-Vegas-Publicity-H-2023.webp)

LIV Las Vegas will feature stadium-like design without any bad seating or obstructed sightline. It will be 50,000 square feet with 62 tables and LIV Beach will be a 35,000 sq ft. dayclub that features 6 bungalows and private plunge pools. Both clubs will feature the DJs and stage tables will go for $25,000.00. However, the clubs are designed so GA can see the DJ booth without issue. Both venues will hold about 2,000 people, half the capacity of most Vegas clubs.

> People want to see, be seen and be entertained. LIV and LIV Beach will not be the biggest \[nightclub and dayclub\] in Vegas but they will have the best experience
> 
> Steven Soffer

How Fontainebleau Las Vegas got to where it should be
-----------------------------------------------------

After the memorable groundbreaking moment, the tower for Fountainebleau Las Vegas went on top in 2008. However with the 2008-2009 global financial crisis approaching and banks closing, in came the lawsuits and construction delays. The aforementioned tower, which was supposed to be Las Vegas’ tallest tower, had to see the rest of the resort and hotel stay at 70 percent completion and construction remain dormant for the next 12 years. Luckily, Soffer and **Fontainebleau Development** partnered up with **Koch Real Estate Investments** to reacquire the property in 2021.

Since the reacquisition of the property, construction restarted and the 3,644-room resort will finally open on December 13th, in time for the 70th anniversary of the [historic classic](https://www.edmtunes.com/2022/04/fontainebleau-hosting-calvin-harris-vintage-culture-more-for-miami-race-nights/) Fontainebleau Miami Beach [hotel](https://www.fontainebleau.com/). Alongside LIV Nightclub and LIV Beach, the fine dining restaurants of **Komodo** and **Papi Steak** will open inside the resort as well in the Spring 2024 season. The owner of these fine dining establishments is the celebrity restaurateur and Las Vegas hospitality entrepreneur David Grutman. Everyone who is a big fan of Las Vegas nightlife will mark December 13th on their calendars as they anticipate the opening of Fontainebleau Las Vegas.

[![Image 4: Fontainebleau Las Vegas Interior Preview](https://www.edmtunes.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Fontainebleau-Las-Vegas-Interior-Preview-1024x563.webp)](https://www.edmtunes.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Fontainebleau-Las-Vegas-Interior-Preview.webp)

===========================================================================================================

Discover the Best Things to Do in Miami: Nightlife Guide & Daytime:
===================================================================

Discover [Miami Nightlife Guide](https://www.vipsouthbeach.com/does-miami-have-good-nightlife/), Miami is a dynamic city that seamlessly blends outstanding nightlife, stunning beaches, cultural diversity, and delectable cuisine. Whether you’re a sun-seeking beach lover, an art enthusiast, or a foodie, Miami offers an abundance of experiences to cater to all tastes. In this article, we’ll explore the top Miami nightlife, attractions and activities that make Miami a must-visit destination. So, get ready to immerse yourself in the magic of the Magic City!

Experience Miami’s Electric Nightlife
-------------------------------------

Miami is internationally acclaimed for its electrifying nightlife scene. Here are a few hotspots to dance the night away:

### 1. Miami Beach Nightclubs:

Experience the legendary [nightlife of South Beach](https://www.vipsouthbeach.com/south-beach-miami-nightlife/) by visiting popular nightclubs such as [LIV nightclub](https://www.vipsouthbeach.com/liv-nightclub-party-package-tickets/) at the Fontainebleau, Nightclub On A [Yacht Boat Party](https://www.vipsouthbeach.com/miami-boat-party-package/), or E11EVEN Miami. The high energy [clubs in Miami](https://www.vipsouthbeach.com/miami-nightlife-entertainment-guide/) host world-renowned DJs and offer a high-energy clubbing experience.

### 2. Brickell’s Rooftop Bars:

Head to Brickell, Miami’s financial district, and enjoy the city views from its trendy rooftop bars. Sip on craft cocktails at venues like Sugar, Juvia, or Area 31 while soaking in the vibrant atmosphere.

### 3. Live Music Venues:

If you prefer live music, Miami offers a variety of venues catering to different genres. Explore the Fillmore Miami Beach, the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts, or the Ball & Chain in Little Havana for a memorable night of music and entertainment.

Soak Up the Sun on Miami’s Pristine Beaches
-------------------------------------------

Miami is renowned for its breathtaking beaches with crystal-clear waters and powdery white sand. Some of the must-visit beaches include:

### 1. South Beach:

Located in the heart of Miami Beach, South Beach is an iconic stretch known for its lively atmosphere, colorful Art Deco buildings, and trendy beachfront bars and clubs.

### 2. Key Biscayne:

Offering a more serene beach experience, Key Biscayne is a tranquil island paradise with beautiful beaches, nature trails, and stunning views of the Miami skyline.

### 3. Crandon Park Beach:

\Situated on Key Biscayne, Crandon Park Beach is perfect for families with its calm waters, picnic areas, and various recreational activities such as kayaking and paddleboarding.

Immerse Yourself in Miami’s Cultural Scene
------------------------------------------

Miami is a melting pot of cultures, which is reflected in its vibrant arts and cultural scene. Here are some highlights:

### 1. Art Deco Historic District:

Take a stroll along Ocean Drive in South Beach and admire the stunning Art Deco architecture. The district is home to over 800 preserved buildings from the 1930s and ’40s, making it a photographer’s paradise.

### 2. Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM):

Located in Downtown Miami, PAMM showcases contemporary art from around the world. The museum’s striking architecture and diverse exhibits make it a must-visit for art enthusiasts.

### 3. Little Havana:

Experience the rich Cuban heritage of Miami by visiting the colorful neighborhood of Little Havana. Explore Calle Ocho (8th Street), indulge in authentic Cuban cuisine, and catch a live salsa performance.

Explore Miami’s Natural Wonders
-------------------------------

Beyond its urban allure, Miami boasts several natural wonders that offer a refreshing escape. Here are a few recommendations:

### 1. Everglades National Park:

Embark on an unforgettable adventure by exploring the Everglades, a unique subtropical wilderness featuring vast wetlands, mangroves, and diverse wildlife. Take an airboat tour and spot alligators, turtles, and exotic birds.

### 2. Vizcaya Museum and Gardens:

Step back in time at the Vizcaya Museum and Gardens, a stunning Italian Renaissance-style villa nestled on Biscayne Bay. The estate’s beautifully landscaped gardens, intricate architecture, and art collections offer a serene retreat.

### 3. Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden:

Discover a tropical paradise at Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden, home to a vast collection of rare plants, butterfly gardens, and tranquil walking trails.

Indulge in Miami’s Culinary Delights
------------------------------------

Miami’s culinary scene is a tantalizing fusion of flavors from around the world. Here are a few must-try food experiences:

### 1. Cuban Cuisine:

Savor the authentic flavors of Cuban cuisine at local eater

ies in Little Havana or explore the famous Versailles Restaurant, known for its delicious Cuban sandwiches and traditional dishes.

### 2. Seafood Delights:

Being a coastal city, Miami is a seafood lover’s paradise. Indulge in fresh catches at renowned seafood restaurants like Joe’s Stone Crab or enjoy a casual waterfront dining experience at Monty’s Raw Bar.

### 3. Wynwood Walls:

Unleash your inner art enthusiast while enjoying Miami’s nightlife at Wynwood Walls. This vibrant neighborhood is home to colorful street art, trendy bars, and live music venues that come alive after dark.

### Miami Nightlife & Daytime Guide

Miami truly has something for everyone, from sun-drenched beaches and cultural landmarks to natural wonders, diverse cuisine, and an exhilarating [Miami nightlife](https://www.vipsouthbeach.com/miaminightlife/). Whether you’re seeking relaxation, exploration, or a lively party scene, the Magic City delivers. Embrace the vibrant energy, immerse yourself in the local culture, and create lasting memories as you discover the best things to do in Miami.

Remember to plan your visit accordingly, considering weather conditions and any specific requirements or restrictions that may be in place. So pack your sunscreen, bring your appetite, and get ready for an unforgettable adventure in Miami, where the sun, art, and nightlife combine for an unparalleled experience.
