17.title: Club Space, E11even, and Heart Transform Miami’s Club District
17.description: Downtown Miami's streets are a stop-and-go roller coaster designed by a renegade gang of evil Disney Imagineers. If you time it wrong — say you arrive right at the end of a Heat game or concert at Bayfront Park (or both, which is a particularly apocalyptic traffic scenario that happens...
17.content:
**Downtown Miami’s streets are a stop-and-go roller coaster designed by a renegade gang of evil Disney Imagineers.** If you time it wrong – say you arrive right at the end of a Heat game or concert at Bayfront Park (or both, which is a particularly apocalyptic traffic scenario that happens at least a few times a year) – you could find yourself sitting on Biscayne Boulevard for hours, surrounded by distracted and possibly drunk drivers who are more invested in their Instagram feeds than the structural health of your rear bumper. Oh, and you’d like a parking spot? That’s cute.

But despite all of the above, some people still forgo Uber and drive downtown. And these are precisely the kind of questionable decision-makers a fellow named Hassan loves to see pull down NW 11th Street, a road that bisects Miami’s only 24-hour club district. It’s a single, sweaty city block that’s home to the clubs Heart, E11even, and the infamous Space – easily the most fanatical nightlife scene in Florida today. And this week, thousands will descend upon it for Miami Music Week, the city’s annual summit of all things dance music that marks an indispensable profit point for these clubs.

Hassan (real last name none of your business) is better known as “New York” in these parts. It’s a nickname inspired by his place of birth. The wiry 61-year-old credits his youthful aura to healthy amounts of marijuana and sex and, he says sweetly after pantomiming both, “a sense of humor.” He does not technically work for any of the nearby clubs. But his job is nonetheless important: to keep the “crackheads and junkies” from breaking into the cars that line his stretch of 11th Street. At 11:30 p.m., he’s armed with only a flashlight. “They stop the generation of money for the clubs,” he says of the break-ins. So he trudges up and down this street till about 6 a.m. In return, he asks only a $5 fee. Or maybe a cigarette. Whatever you can spare, really. His brand of self-starting entrepreneurship is common in this part of town, where everybody seems to have devised a technique to make your wallet lighter.

(His favorite method is to bet passing idiots $20 that he can spell their first and last names despite the fact they have told him neither. If the simpleton accepts the bet, he’ll gleefully begin spelling out _f-i-r-s-t_ and so forth and so on until you pay up, which you should, because he’s incredibly persuasive and it’s cheaper than replacing a car window.)

Will you step up to support New Times this year?
------------------------------------------------

At New Times, we’re small and scrappy — and we make the most of every dollar from our supporters. Right now, we’re $16,750 away from reaching our December 31 goal of $30,000. If you’ve ever learned something new, stayed informed, or felt more connected because of New Times, now’s the time to give back.

Progress to goal

$30,000

### Editor's Picks

*   [Club Space Sues Former Owner Louis Puig Over His Involvement With Heart Nightclub](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/club-space-sues-former-owner-louis-puig-over-his-involvement-with-heart-nightclub-8526036/)
*   [Trifecta of Miami Music Veterans Buy Club Space With Plans to Reinvigorate the Venue](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/trifecta-of-miami-music-veterans-buy-club-space-with-plans-to-reinvigorate-the-venue-8992334/)
*   [E11even Celebrates Two Years of Being a Little Bit of Everything](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/e11even-celebrates-two-years-of-being-a-little-bit-of-everything-8241051/)

Mr. York has been patrolling 11th Street for four years and has lived in Miami for decades. He remembers a time when the only tourists who walked these streets were hopelessly lost and, frankly, terrified.

The area has a long history. In the early 1900s, it was invigorated by a new railroad that shipped goods to the Port of Miami from bustling warehouses on NE 11th Street. But then the Port relocated in 1960. Those warehouses were vacated, and for decades the district was left to rot. Former Miami Mayor Manny Diaz once described 11th Street as a “crack-filled alley.”

But then the new millennium came along, and one brave nightlife entrepreneur, Louis Puig, had a vision for those abandoned warehouses: a club that never closed. It would be raw and dangerous and decidedly un-South Beach. With nothing to lose, the city played along, granting his new Club Space a previously unheard-of 24-hour liquor license.

They came. They danced. It worked.

Five years later, largely at the behest of the late Miami-Dade County Commissioner Arthur Teele, the area was christened an entertainment district. The endgame was to create a mainland tourist haven with restaurants, art galleries, the works. A little more than 4,000 days later, Teele’s vision is closer than ever to realization. But as was evident during a recent 12-hour visit, 11th Street is still a long way from family-friendly – more Fury Road than Lincoln Road.

![Image 1: A DJ controls the music from the console in a nightclub, with an ice bucket containing alcohol bottles](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/ww-media/mediaserver/mia/2017-12/feature1-1-71e90e3fbcfb5674.webp)

With the help of music director Travis Rogers, Heart has showcased world-class DJs like Boys Noize (pictured) and Nicole Moudaber. Most nights, Heart doesn’t get going till at least 4 a.m.

Photo by Chris Carter

**If you’re looking for a nightclub on 11th Street, you have several options.** There’s Space, the first of the 11th Street venues, as well as two relative newcomers, E11even and Heart. There are also a few smaller places to get a drink, including Floyd and the Corner.

But for all of the above, 2 a.m. is a bit on the early side, which is why three young men visiting from New York City are currently huddled around a yellow fire hydrant and wearing the unmistakable look of disappointment. Their flight home is in a few hours. Hoping to redeem their perhaps disappointing trip, they decided to stop by Heart for one last hurrah. Sadly, the 20-year-olds struck out in all metrics of nightlife success and are now cashless, sober, and, unless one of them has a thing for yellow fire hydrants, won’t be getting laid tonight.

“We listen to mostly EDM,” one of the New Yorkers says, “and the music here is, like, not at all EDM.” The boys are right. They probably would have been happier in Miami Beach, where mainstream DJs still draw thousands into big-room clubs such as LIV and Story. But for all of its success across the bay, the EDM boom has never found firm footing on 11th Street. And Heart’s music director, Travis Rogers, would like to keep it that way. “At the end of the day, my goal was to book stuff I like,” he says a week later over the phone. Tonight’s headliner is Damian Lazarus, an electronic artist known for being more of a mystic shaman than a DJ. He occasionally shows up to a set dressed somewhere between Abu from _Aladdin_ and a Russian Orthodox LSD salesman.

In other words: like, not at all EDM.

But Lazarus won’t go on till at least 4 a.m. Right now, around 2:30, things are still in first gear. The second-story dance floor – spread out beneath a ceiling of lush vines – has a light sway to it, more wheat in a gentle breeze than popcorn in a skillet. That chaos won’t happen until much later. Heart is unapologetically for night owls, and Saturdays sometimes extend to 9 p.m. Sunday.

The club is a bit of an underdog story. In its previous life, it was called Nocturnal and was a semiformidable room that nipped at the heels of Space when it opened in 2005. But Sunday, September 18, 2011, an argument broke out on the terrace. Bottles were thrown, insults were hurled, and a gun was pulled. The packed room stampeded down the stairs in terror. When the dust cleared, six were wounded and a 26-year-old North Miami man was dead. Nocturnal shut down shortly after and remained shuttered for years. A club named Bekkoi tried to take over the venue in August 2015 but lasted only months.

And then Heart opened September 11, 2015, with almost no warning or advance press. The club has since reinvented itself, remodeling its first floor and resurrecting the second-story rooftop, where a capacity of about 600 can enjoy the sunrise to the sounds of dance-music gods like John Digweed and Nicole Moudaber.

Now Heart and Rogers, having booked heavy-hitters such as Thomas Gold, Marco Carola, and Markus Schulz, are heading into their second Miami Music Week with confidence. But the club still has an uphill battle to face in both fierce competition from its neighbor, Space, and Art Teele’s grand vision of downtown, a future evident in the sounds of construction mere blocks away. Rogers is optimistic about the immediate future, but to him, the bigger picture looks bleak. “I don’t think the nightlife future is going to be huge in downtown Miami in, say, ten years or even existent,” Rogers says,”unless it’s inside a hotel.”

![Image 2: Nightclub is filled with partygoers under a canopy and disco ball](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/ww-media/mediaserver/mia/2017-12/feature1-3-0f06c641e73d8930.webp)

Club Space

**Four a.m. is about the time when your night is heading in one of two directions.** You are either (1) in it for the long haul, resigned to see this thing through till the bitter end, possibly, if you’re lucky, with the help of a beautiful stranger. Or you are (2) bleeding from the eyeball.

Sadly, option number two is happening just outside E11even. A man in skintight white jeans and gold sneakers is holding court before an audience of attentive bouncers. He is explaining his side of things and, no, he will not calm down and, yes, he wants to press charges. It’s unclear what started the fight but very clear who won it. The poor guy’s right eye is already plump and purplish. A single tear of blood funnels down between his collar bones and into his shirt.

This is not how it was meant to be. Just ask that gentleman over there, the one sporting a leather vest and a shiny newsboy cap that looks like it’s made from the carcass of several disco balls. “I’m from a different time in New York, where we weren’t so aggressive with the girls, where you danced with space,” says the man, who prefers to remain anonymous. Now in his early 40s and a doctor by day, he’s been clubbing in Miami for decades. He was here when Space opened in 2000. And, let him tell you, those were the days. Before he moved here, he was partying in the legendary era of Peter Gatien’s New York City, a truly sinister playground of flesh. And it wasn’t just the music or the drugs that made it unique – though, in all honesty, the drugs didn’t hurt – there was something more metaphysical. “I wish I could take people back in time… There was sort of a code we grew up with, the way you behave in there, the way you act.

> The clubs were sanctuaries of self-expression that offered a catharsis from racism and oppression.

[Tweet this](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=The%20clubs%20were%20sanctuaries%20of%20self-expression%20that%20offered%20a%20catharsis%20from%20racism%20and%20oppression.)

“It was just,” he sighs as if remembering a lost love. “It was just great.”

This all might seem a bit dramatic – like the dance-music-saved-my-life spiel heard all too often from high-schoolers returning from their first Ultra Music Festival. But it’s important to consider the history of the modern nightclub and its relationship to dance music. Separate your preconceived notions of glowstick, Bieber-esque EDM from the pioneering roots of early house music, a dangerous sound that grew from the ashes of disco into warehouses full of people whom society considered far too strange or weird or black or gay or black and gay. These clubs were more than an excuse to get high and fuck people and take selfies. They were sanctuaries of self-expression that offered a catharsis from racism, oppression, and all the milquetoast Wally-and-the-Beaver-looking motherfuckers who dominated pop culture at the time.

These oases existed across the United States in the ’80s and ’90s in cities like Detroit, Chicago, New York, and especially [Miami, where ’90s South Beach clubs like Salvation, Amnesia, and Velvet brought together gays and straights of all races and cultures.](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/long-before-the-vip-section-dance-music-in-miami-was-for-the-oppressed-8318611) They gave this city the identity it still cashes in on today.

Yes, it can seem silly now, hearing evangelical testimonials like the one above, but it was serious back then because outside of those clubs, danger lurked in the form of closed fists, hissed slurs, and maybe worse if you caught the eye of the wrong group of good old boys. And while you’re thinking about this history, it’s also important to consider the contemporary sociopolitical climate of our country and ask yourself: “Gee, could such a place of unconditional acceptance and empathy have any sort of use in society today?” And if your answer is a big fat yup, well, we have good news, Miami. That place is being built – uh, rebuilt- right this very moment.

But it’s going to need your help.

![Image 3: Three men pose in front of the Club Space building](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/ww-media/mediaserver/mia/2017-12/feature1-2-fcc716712017ef16.webp)

David Sinopoli (left), Davide Danese, and Coloma Kaboomsky are leading an audacious takeover of the famed Club Space.

Photo by Chris Carter

**The sunrise is as universal a routine as this planet has ever known, but it still sneaks up on you somehow.** Maybe it’s like many of life’s big moments: love, children, sex, doughnuts – things we experience that almost always blindside us with their greatness or scare us with their power. Forgive me. Things begin to feel sentimental around 7 a.m., particularly when you haven’t had breakfast yet. Scientists have actually found short-term sleep deprivation – around 12 hours’ worth – to be a quick method of alleviating symptoms of depression in somewhere around half of the sad little mice they tested. It’s temporary, though, and generally wears off after a good night’s sleep.

At 7 a.m., clubgoers’ brains are full of a neurotransmitter called adenosine, which slowly builds all day, eventually causing the familiar sensation we know as sleepiness. But if that poor adenosine is ignored – especially by a big room of people dancing to loud, pulsing music – some truly weird and incredible things start happening.

In the final moments of the night’s darkness, there is an anticipatory buzz in the humid air of Space’s Terrace. Light begins to creep through the translucent roof, dim at first before reaching a brilliant white. There are those who planned for this moment (the ones reaching into purses and pulling out sunglasses) and those who didn’t (the ones staring at the roof as if aliens had just burst through it, anal probes in hand).

Club Space has long been known as the place to be in Miami when night gives way to day. This has been true since it opened in 2000 in its original location, a one-story warehouse a block east from where it stands now. The club was a ground-breaker in many ways. It was the first true 24-hour nightlife concept in the city and the leader in gambling on Miami’s then desolate and unsexy downtown.

Space’s founder, [Louis Puig, described his club thusly in a 2013 open letter](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/louis-puig-it-is-true-i-sold-club-space-6447799): “Space was ahead of its time; it was the antiestablishment to the South Beach commercial VIP clubs with the French velvet-rope attitude that unfortunately still prevails today. Space was underground and so separated from the norm that few gave it or me a chance of success.”

Of course, there were hiccups. After Space earned a druggy reputation, [the DEA raided it in August 2003 and arrested 11 people, including two employees, on drug-related charges.](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/party-on-6346934) But the club remained open, and if anything, the drug hype only added to its mystique. Eventually, other clubs invested in 11th Street and the lucrative 24-hour operation licenses. It wasn’t long before thousands of revelers flooded the area each weekend. But that wasn’t exactly a good thing for Space.

Soon crowds shifted to the unsavory. The club’s staff, bouncers in particular, gained a nasty and abusive reputation. In 2013, when Puig announced he was selling his venue, the same club kids who had helped build Space wouldn’t be caught dead inside it.

The new owners, the wildly successful Miami nightlife duo of Justin Levine and Roman Jones, kept the club afloat, but Space never regained its sheen or inclusive reputation. It became better known for lawsuits than parties. [There was one case against Puig himself for allegedly violating a noncompete agreement by working with Heart](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/club-space-sues-former-owner-louis-puig-over-his-involvement-with-heart-nightclub-8526036) (the case has since been settled). And [there was a particularly hilarious suit with an airplane banner company that flew a sign over downtown Miami, pleading, “Club Space – Please Pay Your Banner Bill!”](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/club-space-sues-airplane-banner-company-over-an-aerial-message-8432856) (the case is still open). By the end of last year, rumors swirled that Space was on death watch, liable to close its doors at any moment.

That wasn’t the case, but Space was in rough shape. Levine and Jones were weighing options. Still, they saw potential in the club and knew that, under the right leadership, it might be able to rise again to the top of Miami nightlife. So Levine called an old friend, David Sinopoli, the cofounder of Miami’s III Points Festival and music director at Bardot.

For Sinopoli, it was both a thrilling and terrifying prospect. On one hand, it’s Space, but on the other, it’s _Space_. “The reputation to me, especially over the last few years, is a little bit of a gift and a curse,” Sinopoli says. “In some sense, I would have loved to have the infrastructure with a brand-new slate to start my first club, but the opportunity with this place – if you can turn it around – there isn’t a real ceiling to it.” So he said yes, and by December, he had his very own club. He wasted little time assembling a team. [To help in the monumental task of remolding Space, he tapped Davide Danese and Coloma Kaboomsky](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/trifecta-of-miami-music-veterans-buy-club-space-with-plans-to-reinvigorate-the-venue-8992334), two local promoters and music directors who helped turn Treehouse into one of the few successful underground dance clubs in Miami Beach. None of them is over age 40, by the way.

> Space will live or die based on one basic but very tricky thing: Can it shed its noxious reputation?

[Tweet this](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Space%20will%20live%20or%20die%20based%20on%20one%20basic%20but%20very%20tricky%20thing%3A%20Can%20it%20shed%20its%20noxious%20reputation%3F)

That’s rare in Miami nightlife, where for so many years the city’s elite clubs were controlled by a tight circle of industry veterans. But Sinopoli, Danese, and Kaboomsky – or the “Space Invaders,” as they’ve taken to calling themselves – are anything but establishment. And it’s hard not to see their takeover as a tiny revolution in Miami club culture, especially when you hear some of their ideas, which range from the brilliantly simple to the wildly ambitious. Let’s start with the latter: There will be a complete remodeling of Space’s first floor, a cavernous room traditionally devoted to hip-hop and open format. The new ground floor will showcase live music ranging from local artists to midsize touring acts who have struggled to find an adequate venue since the closing of downtown’s Grand Central. Space’s adjacent club, which opened in June 2015 under the name Libertine, has been rebranded as Floyd, a jazzy spot that will host everything from the traditional quartet to spoken word and academic lectures.

On the simple side of the spectrum, Space has retrained its staff to use more welcoming language, such as “please” and “thank you.” ATM fees and water prices have been slashed. Free cafecito and flowers are handed out at sunrise. A nonalcoholic menu featuring all-natural juices is forthcoming. And to the Terrace they’ve added – wait for it – seats. “That was a key,” Kaboomsky says. “If you expect people to be there for 14 hours, they’ve got to be able to sit down.” Again, brilliantly simple, sure, but these concepts are unique in their motivation, which puts profit behind customer experience – or, as Kaboomsky says, “making sure people don’t feel like they’re being fucked.”

That’s big, because in the eyes of the Invaders, Space will live or die based on one basic but very tricky thing: whether it can shed its noxious reputation. “We understood this in the first week, but we were bleeding money everywhere because there were old habits,” Sinopoli says.

December was difficult for the new owners. “Some of the staff was really down because they hadn’t been making money in a little bit. Some people really weren’t happy that we were there.” But by New Year’s Eve, things began to turn around, and Space started to feel like home.

In the short term, things at 34 NE 11th St. are shifting into place. But the bigger picture raises uncertainty. The looming shadow cast upon downtown Miami by powerful developers grows wider every year. The $1.6 billion orgy of condos, retail stores, hotels, and apartments known as Miami Worldcenter has already pushed out venues such as Grand Central and Mekka.

For now, Sinopoli is confident in the contract he and his team punched up, which gives them a guaranteed five years and a five-year option to renew. “If they end up ever doing anything there, which is always an option, we have clauses that protect us,” he says. But he admits even the strongest contract isn’t impervious to the whims of the rich and powerful.

Right now, though, as the sun rises higher over Space’s Terrace, the future couldn’t seem further away. There is only one concern in the minds of the twirling, sun-kissed occupants of Space. And it’s not what will happen in ten years or ten minutes or even ten seconds. It is the now that matters – the glorious, irresponsible now.

“You know, we’re really going for a utopian place,” Kaboomsky says. “We don’t have romantic visions of a utopian civilization – we know it’s not possible. But if you take it and put it inside of a building, it might be possible… even if it’s for only ten hours on a Saturday night.”

![Image 4: Man with dark hair, light skin, wearing a dark suit with a colorful tie, in front of a background of blue light](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/ww-media/mediaserver/mia/2017-12/feature1-4-5abb9adc0cbba8d6.webp)

Nightlife veteran and New York native Dennis DeGori is the mastermind behind E11even.

**What do tourists dream about when they dream about Miami?**

Do they skip around in fields of $100 bills, hopping to and fro on lily pads of Brazilian butt-lifts? Do they drift softly down a river of fizzy champagne on Gucci inner tubes while Pitbull passes them mojitos? Is every delicious sin in modern history competing for their attention?

If so, what must that tourist feel upon entering E11even? Is it quite literally a dream come true?

At 8 a.m., it can feel that way, surreal as if you tripped and fell into your TV screen and are now trapped in a never-ending music video. Time is meaningless inside E11even, a two-story fortress of concrete with an exterior that does little justice to the feast of the senses inside. The atmosphere is a perpetual state of 4 a.m. Unlike at Space, nobody here cares about the position of the sun. Topless dancers bounce and spin to the sounds of big-room EDM. Everyone is well dressed and has the facial expression of someone at the apex of a roller coaster – that _tick-tick-tick_ right before the big drop.

Take every nightclub concept that has ever existed and throw it into a pot. Give it a stir. Soak a stack of money in the world’s most expensive Russian vodka, light the bills on fire, and then toss them into the pot. Grab the nearest available famous rapper, take him by the ankles, and use him as a stirring spoon. If E11even had a recipe, it would look something like that.

Dennis DeGori, the creator of this strange land, has a go-to tag line for the common question: Just what in hell is this place? “It’s exactly what you think it is,” he’ll tell you plainly, which doesn’t make a whole lot of sense but sounds pretty cool. For DeGori, a 35-year nightlife veteran, E11even is a culmination of just about everything he’s ever seen in a nightclub that’s intrigued him. “I just wanted to set out to create something unique, exciting, theatrical, artistic, and, above all, fun,” he says. “An immersive experience.”

E11even, which celebrated its third anniversary in February, is nothing if not immersive. It features everything from aerial performances to New Year’s Eve bashes hosted by Drake. Oh, and the club literally never closes. Ever. It stays open 24 hours a day, seven days a week. You can also walk up to the bar and order breakfast in the morning. Get the SoBe wrap – a warm bundle of egg whites, spinach, mushrooms, and cheddar cheese – and the fellow to your left might stare longingly at the plate until you offer him a bite.

### Related

*   [Eclectic “Women in Jazz” Fest Comes to Miami Beach Bandshell This Weekend](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/eclectic-women-in-jazz-fest-comes-to-miami-beach-bandshell-this-weekend-40503484/)

Before E11even came around, most folks emerged from 29 NE 11th St. stinking of regret, along with other less desirable fluids. It was called Goldrush back then, and it was a strip club not exactly known for its elegance. The club closed in April 2013. Its Yelp page, still preserved online, is rich with first-person tales of nights gone horribly awry and accusations of overcharging. One time, the prominent lawyer and founder of the Ticket Clinic, Mark S. Gold, sued the strip club because he claimed it had gotten him too drunk, forcing him to have “a complete loss of judgment [and] rational thought,” at which point he apparently spent more than $18,000.

Despite that, DeGori says, he had his eye on the property for more than a decade. When it finally hit the market, he pounced. “I saw it in my mind’s eye,” he says. “Long before it was halfway built, I could stand in the middle of what we were doing, in the dirt, and just see it taking form.” But even DeGori admits E11even’s success has surpassed his expectations. In only three years, it has become one of Miami’s most popular clubs, doing what popular clubs do best: earning a fuck-ton of money.

The E11even universe revolves around money, whether it’s being tossed casually onto the backs of twerking dancers or filling up the club’s fat bank account. E11even nabbed an “honorable mention” on _Nightclub & Bar_‘s list of the top-earning clubs of 2014, cracking the top ten with around $20 million in profit despite the fact that it hadn’t been open for a full 12 months. Being diplomatic, DeGori won’t say whether he thinks 2016’s revenue will be enough to bump LIV from the position of Miami’s highest-grossing club, a title it’s held since 2012. But business certainly seems to be booming.

DeGori hopes to expand E11even beyond Miami and fears encroaching developers like a lion fears a housecat. He embraces the vision of a highly developed downtown and welcomes the day tourists roam the streets in search of more than just a dance floor. But, of course, he’ll still welcome the ones seeking a good time. “I definitely see E11even here for the next 25 years.” And in the next quarter-century, he better see you. “No matter when you walk through the doors, we’ll be ready for you. It will be an experience.”

![Image 5: A crowded dance floor in a nightclub full of people, yellow and blue lights, and a second level](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/ww-media/mediaserver/mia/2017-12/feature1-5-8d61e1dae94a1ebe.webp)

The 24/7 party palace E11even has quickly become one of the city’s most popular clubs.

**Many questions hit you when the night finally ends and you walk out onto the street one last time,** surveying a slightly sadder world through spread fingers. One of those questions might be: Why? Perhaps it hits you quickly, or maybe it waits till you’re alone, head smooshed in a pillow sandwich.

Why – did I spend all my money; do I smell like gasoline; am I going home with this man who looks, in the natural light of morning, more and more like a hobbit with each passing moment?

Why do we dress up, primp in front of mirrors, spend hours on our feet in uncomfortable shoes, our only reward sometimes bloodthirsty headaches and regretful text messages? And then do it all again in a matter of days? You can ride this question far back in time, all the way to the ancient Romans and even further if you’d like. We are not the first generation to spend our nights so restlessly, and we won’t be the last. We are social animals, and to gather and play is essential to our survival as a species. Put us on different continents with nothing but rocks and sticks, and we’ll somehow find one another if you give us long enough. Give us even longer and we’ll eventually create a place like 11th Street.

> What a silly waste of time and money and brain cells — such an utterly ridiculous mating ritual.

[Tweet this](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=What%20a%20silly%20waste%20of%20time%20and%20money%20and%20brain%20cells%20%26mdash%3B%20such%20an%20utterly%20ridiculous%20mating%20ritual.)

Miami can feel lonely, right? It’s weird. Everyone seems to belong to some tribe that’s off-limits to you. The city’s fantastical opulence is always, somehow, just out of reach. You look around and all you see is people having more fun than you. But there are certain places – and substances – that even the playing field, so to speak.

Maybe you hate the nightclub. How sad and vain and loud and expensive, you say. What a silly waste of time and money and brain cells. Such an utterly ridiculous mating ritual we have created for ourselves.

And it’s easy to see things that way, especially from the outside looking in. But even if Heart or Space or E11even isn’t your thing – even if you’d rather spend 12 hours in a dentist’s waiting room than set foot inside a club – you should disregard your assumptions and try it. Just once. Shimmy onto the dance floor and close your eyes. Sweat. Think about life and how little sense the whole thing makes. Do you realize you were the one sperm out of hundreds of millions that made it inside the egg? Now open your eyes. Look to your left and to your right. Feel connected. Consider the fact that it’s 80 degrees in March. Think about the last person you loved and the way her hair felt against your face. You realize Earth is spinning at more than 1,000 mph, right? Like, right now! Deep breath. One more time.

Now go home. And get some fucking sleep.

However, I did not anticipate that the nightclub would be so gorgeous! LIV is an upscale club that contains an eye-catching decor! They have a downstairs and upstairs where all clubgoers can frequent, which I loved! They didn't implement a nonsensical system where only VIPs can have access upstairs while regular admission attendees must stay on the floor. Clubgoers and a lion like myself should have free reign in the nightclub jungle! While upstairs, I saw several beautiful booth-style sections made out of leather. I believe they have one bar upstairs. Downstairs, they have three bars. Throughout the night, I saw several custodians mopping up spilled drinks, which impressed me because spilled drinks in a packed nightclub are hazardous and unavoidable. LIV has a nice-sized dance floor in the club's center and some roped-off sections behind it. It was a pleasure to see a large dancefloor in a nightclub in this era of section-hungry, money-hungry nightclubs. Nightclubs are supposed to be festive, and nothing destroys a festive nightclub more than too many sections where everyone is sitting down and people-watching. The sound system knocks, and the halo over the dance floor and lighting are visually stimulating. Nightclubs typically get hot due to the body heat of many people nearby and no ventilation. However, the heat wasn't an issue at LIV because they had one the most frigid air-conditioners I ever felt; they must have had the air conditioning on the "South Pole" setting because I had a few chilly moments despite wearing a turtle neck, blazer, and fedora. I would rather a nightclub have an air conditioner that is too cold than not cold enough, so keep that chilly air blowing. Come Summertime, the air conditioning will be perfect. The white DJ who opened for Metro Boomin could have easily been a headliner himself! I asked a pleasant bouncer the DJ's name, but he didn't know. Metro Boomin headlined and had one of the most moving entrances I have seen, and he handled his business on the ones and twos. When Metro Boomin returns, which he will because he's in the rotation, I highly recommend people show up, especially Hip Hop lovers! LIV is the truth, and I will return when they have hip-hop performers and DJs and R&B-themed nights! Pro tip: I returned to LIV a week after this review, and everything I said holds. However, it was about a fourth of the crowd there, and it could not come even remotely close to my first time attending. It is paramount that you go on a night where Metro Boomin or an entertainer who has a large fan base performs. Koryn G.

Yelp

Went to go see John Summit and loved the energy. Amazing vibes! Loved the huge screens setup behind the main bar. Enjoyed getting to view the stage from the upper level as well. Service was pretty good. Drinks were decent there too!

![Image 74: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/Z5oNALToyRUrArUdoBBZCA/180s.jpg)

Jaime B.

Yelp

Great place to go with friends and have a good time, the vive is outstanding but lil expensive, service is good and fast , drinks are ok but enjoyable, plenty of parking but don't forget to validate your ticket at the front so you don't pay in your way out.

![Image 75: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/W9GOfZYsmtTz95cTMmjCew/180s.jpg)

Tammie K.

Yelp

Bought tickets to John summit and they denied us entry. People waited hours and couldn't get in even with a ticket. Bouncers were nonchalant and came off extremely entitled. Don't bother coming to this club on a busy weekend because they will not honor your $100+ ticket. Disputed the charge on my credit card and got my money back tho

![Image 76: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/OXPICHHqqUv6UlK5OZIitw/180s.jpg)

Shar S.

Yelp

Came here to see Busta Rhymes and the place was packed! Drinks were served quickly, and the vibe was high energy. I liked the way the club looked in the light, too (I had come here once before to work an event). Would definitely come back to see more acts here!

![Image 77: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/HpnaQnNxHK06oeH5TlqE9w/180s.jpg)

Juan D.

Yelp

Terrible. Over two and a half hours waiting in line even though I had paid entrance I was treated like I was going in there for free or asking them for a favor to allow us in. Not worth it so many better options in Vegas. No wonder the entire hotel is dead no guests. Chawww

![Image 78: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/05Lz_ZvTp7kdY5Hw9rUGmg/180s.jpg)

Jamin B.

Yelp

Oversold tickets. I get that it's John summit and that it's memorial weekend but even clubs in Miami, LA, and NY, have a better and more efficient line and customer service than this . It's quite funny because when I talked to a staff member, he told me that "tickets are simply prioritized (which the aren't) not guaranteed," saying it was part of their terms and conditions, which is I don't see (hope some lawyer gets on this, easy money and some shady ass promotion) so there is literally no point in getting tickets. He also essentially told me to get a refund and that it wouldn't be an issue... I'm guessing this has happened many times before. Felt awfully like a scam to just promote, not really give a shit about their customers at the need of the day. This is also super disrespectful to the artists for creating a venue that really makes consumers feel like they're wasting their time, which is not what the artist intended because they are decent people, and also the people who travel to see this and go out of their way to make it part of their well earned vacationHad to wait an hour in line... to move 5 feet...still waiting, and the staff is extremely entitled, almost answering everything with a condescending tone. Idk, other hotel staff don't act like this, whoever was the hiring manager definitely screwed up when it came to foreseeing staff behavior evolving into nothing short of straight up rudeness and indifference. Security and staff should treat people with respect, especially customers; just because you create a little demand for an artist does not make you entitled to treat people like shit, especially those who pay you. Maybe it was just this crew, but regardless, it was interesting to see how the entire hotel was empty besides the club... I guess they gotta pretend to keep something looking busy and productive. Most likely, people who vote positively are people who promote the club, are friends with people who promote the club, or got a table. GA can zing off essentially. If you're going to establish yourself as a luxury hotel and club, at least have a bit of class. Who expected the new kid on the block to be such an asshat.

![Image 79: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/TrvNUn4JRCnpyyMKquOlmA/180s.jpg)

Kaitlin J.

Yelp

Worst nightclub I've ever been to in Vegas. My party of six paid for expedited entry ($100 ticket) and when we got in they said we couldn't enter the dance floor without a table or some sort of VIP wristband. Never heard of that, especially after paying, they treated us like we got in for free and they were doing us a favor. Such a joke. The staff was incredibly rude. Left shortly after the opener came out the vibe was so low at that point. We had to stand on the outskirts in the foot traffic from all the bar areas, the most annoying spot to be.

![Image 80: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/clvlg2eiUESo0S9EqR_WPw/180s.jpg)

Breanna R.

Yelp

came here to see an artist. was walking out because it was too crowded. as I was exiting a "security gaurd" pushed me and said "move bro" and continues pushing me. I tumbled over and was cut my someones outfit. VERY disappointed and will never come back here. to top it off as I was waiting in the club lobby security tackled a club goer and the pushed me and my friend again. if you want to be pushed and mistreated, this is the perfect place. I can not believe he put his hands on me. I am very sober and can be compliant if he just asked me to go the other way. COMPLETELY disrespectful. I am so embarrassed!

![Image 81: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/k1lvXoskuzaVos4pP28S_g/180s.jpg)

Courtnee A.

Yelp

This venue is beautiful! We saw cloonee's opening night here and the lines were quick, and the guest list girls were on top of their jobs. The bathrooms are beautiful We paid 41 for a Red Bull, water, and a ginger ale though so that was not fun Also I was promised open bar for females until 1 am and when I asked the bartender they said someone was supposed to give me a ticket/wristband. Oh well Cloonee's set was generic and it sucked because I've never seen him and was really excited to come-this isn't the club's fault though but oh well! Also it is FREEZING cold in here so dress appropriately and wear a parka and snow boots

Melissa S.

Yelp

How's the bouncer gonna tell me he'll let me get back in if I go to the br real quick and then the other bouncer goes well that's not me so no get out???? Get new staff yall weird fr thinking you guys are above everyone. $25 a drink??! Go somewhere else

Dee E.

Yelp

Arin literally gave me the best experience for visiting Vegas thank you so much!!! Anyone who's in Vegas ask for Arin

Amanda I.

Yelp

Lawrence "one of the supervisors" and the rest of the management/team overall need to retake an identification class. Denied me based on my "jawline" difference. Had my ID rescanned in the casino downstairs by a worker & personally escorted back into the club just to get denied again. Super discriminating. And no I was not drunk nor disrespectful, clearly denied because they over sell tickets & don't know to run a club with a big artist properly.

![Image 82: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/zxnjklTrJjdKYPmxjMYAhA/180s.jpg)

Greg G.

Yelp

This club is a train wreck stay away. Greedy promoters oversell tickets so even if you pay top dollar for a ticket you will stand in like for hours and still possibly not get in. Rude, unhelpful staff. Unorganized, dysfunctional club.

![Image 83: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/yvdc8fRbRDaetfxsiMKdtQ/180s.jpg)

Marta S.

Yelp

Not recommended, staff is rude , long wait for service. And for that price you can find a better option on the strip

![Image 84: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/Zq1h2JuZiE2GtxA0UXDdJA/180s.jpg)

Chantal G.

Yelp

Definitely have a lot to learn from other clubs in town who make a smooth entry. The entrance services is really really bad, under staffed so the lines is too slow or doesn't move at all. Maybe it was this night but it was unbearable. I found the drinks are overpriced compare to the other club in town. The club is set for mostly VIP setting since the whole club is surrounded with VIP table downstairs to downstairs, though you can stand on the stairs to view the surrounding and you got a pretty good view, the so suppose to be the dance floor is very small. The night I was there is for Gabito Ballesteros however we didn't make it to wait for here it was 2 am she never showed up and we decided to live the place, it was just too packed and the music was ok for a non Spanish person, my mistake. PROS: The place is new so maybe nice to visit, nice set up for VIP seating if you want to pay that price Its very open to move around up and down the stairs and the stairs are big You can view the DJ platform very well from most of the VIP tables and while standing on the stairs I like the lighting set up, nice design Cons: The place is mainly set for VIP tables, if you are not seating in one of the VIP tables or have VIP access you have to stand on the stairs so see anything father away Very small dance floor Very poor service and understaffed Too long to wait outside if you are on a guestlist, you need to stand at least 1h:30 mn standing on line, only one person to check in all lines on a busy Saturday night Suggestions: On Busy Saturday night line up at 9 pm to guarantee you will be getting in if you are on guestlist Either way if you are there on a busy night with a popular DJ you will be waiting on line for one and half hour. In my opinion, its not worth it for right now maybe I will come back in one year and hope they will figure it out by then.

![Image 85: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/iUvzYg1eimIr-SG_XF9Vmg/180s.jpg)

Melinda E.

Yelp

I was very disappointed with this venue . It wasn't like the experience I've had in Miami . My friends and I were on the guest list and got there at a decent time. The line was wrapped around to idk where and we wasted about 3hrs of our lives waiting to get in . Once we almost got to the front , security tells us it's at capacity . By the time they did this it was about 1:30am & of course a fight broke out . Overall, the experience was nothing but chaos.

![Image 86: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/Z-vkqaI6b52sE81MzSOorQ/180s.jpg)

Denielle L.

Yelp

Avoid. We were on the guest list and we had to wait in a LONG line in the cold. The ppl that were meeting us (who were also on the guest list) were told they couldn't come up to even get in lin me with us. We understand that it's busy but then they said it was $200 for males on the guest list. Forget that!

![Image 87: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/B3LhoSRPnTELsrEJML0mHw/180s.jpg)

Patricia Y.

Yelp

LIV management oversold tickets for John Summit and withheld me from entry. They refused to provide a refund or any kind of reimbursement despite their inability to fulfill their promise. I have seen countless of others being taken advantage of this way. They are asking for a class action lawsuit.

Brittany C.

Yelp

I was excited to go to LIV beach club this past Saturday to see John Sunmit perform. I had booked a day bed to ensure that my friends and I would have bottle service and food accessible since it was going to be a long day. We let the promoter know we would be arriving at 130pm as our flight all landed at 1130. We arrived at 125pm and alerted the promoter to our arrival. When we got to the front of the table line, the staff at LIV stated that they had decided to sell our table to someone else without letting us know. They said sorry and threw 4 drink coupons at us. We said this wasn't acceptable as we had already paid the deposit. The staff made us stand in the heat for about 45 min and they finally put us at a table shoved in a corner (not the day bed we had purchased). The service was so slow and bad that our table neighbors had to flag people down so that we could place our order. Meanwhile this is taking so long John summit is about to go on and our beverages still haven't arrived. Our promoter was aware of what was happening and attempting to make calls to correct the issue, but the staff at lIV simply did not seem to care. The management did not take care of any food or drinks. In fact they wouldn't let us leave until we purchased a second bottle even though the club was closing. Additionally they did not apply the deposit that had already been paid, and have not refunded me. We spend that night and Sunday night at XS and had a wonderful experience with our bottle service there. The staff was friendly and attentive and we wanted for nothing. Do yourself a favor, no matter who is playing at LIV, don't go. It's not worth the headache and being treated like garbage. Check out somewhere like XS.

![Image 88: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/yXlDrSolaE6V9afdrX-6Ew/180s.jpg)

Marry A.

Yelp

Such a cool venue.. my sister and I made it on the guest list to see a hip hop show... go here! So classy and fun!

![Image 89: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/5R7gFBwvt6vY2IdF_lhcjQ/180s.jpg)

Vanessa A.

Yelp

I've been to LIV about three times now and every time I've had a better experience than the last most recently I saw Myke Towers and the Altura DJs on Cinco de Mayo, and I was lucky enough to actually meet Myke after the performance inside the Fontainebleau, which was a huge plus!!! But it is a newer club and it's important to be aware of all the rules to ensure that you have a good time. 1. I always recommend getting on the guestlist for the events that you're going to. If you need a good promoter I recommend Mark W. (@sincityswagss on Instagram) he's super reliable and communicative to help you have a good time. If you're on the guest list, I recommend arriving to Fontainebleau by 10 p.m. Even if the doors don't open until 10:30, arrival by 10 p.m. will get you in the line before it's super long and ensure that the process goes very smoothly. If it's an event with drink tickets you'll have no issue getting your tickets and the staff are typically very helpful at that time. \*\*A lot of people in past reviews probably are complaining about the long lines because they got through after 10:30 or even closer to 11 and I'm telling you....it's crazy how many people are arriving AT 10:30 and how much longer the line can get in such a short amount of time. It's insane.\*\* I recommend arriving on time if you are on the guest list because the cover charge is a pretty penny for sure especially for men. 2. When you get in the club it's definitely a gorgeous atmosphere. I always recommend taking photos at the LIV sign when you get in, in the bathroom, on the dance floor and all over. Enjoy some time on the dance floor if you can BUT I will let you know that the staff is VERY strict with letting people into the dance floor as the place starts to get more packed. Each time that I've went, I've left the dance floor to go to the bathroom or to throw away my drink and we are not always let back onto the dance floor. This was an issue the first time that we went (I didn't realize it, and my boyfriend was not able to rejoin the group of us on the dance floor). But it's just to be expected because they are very intense about enforcing the capacity down there. They will let you back into the dance floor if you have a wristband which I'm assuming is for a table. But if not then you might have to find another spot to enjoy the show. I typically go for behind the DJ booth or closer to the front. But on the left and right sides it definitely is not that spacious and not very comfortable. If you can afford a table here then go for it but you don't necessarily need to get one to have a good time. I've gone with one to three other people before and had a great time. 3. Drink prices are expensive ($20+) but it's the strip so it should be expected. it could be worse, try Omnia or XS Drink tickets are given out at some events but not always so just keep that in mind when you go. Pre-gaming is definitely a must 4. Keep in mind that the performers are never going to come out at the time that the doors open. Vegas norms. When we went to see Myke Towers, the doors opened at 10:30 and he didn't come out until 2am. We almost left beforehand, but stayed n it was worthwhile. We also went to see Gabito Ballesteros, and we left before he could come out since he came out around the same time as well. So make sure to do your research, and if you struggle with staying up that late, then keep that in mind before you commit to going. But the performers put on a great show. I really enjoyed seeing Myke Towers on 5/ 5. Liv is like the only club I go to on the strip because they play Latin music/work with Altura so I'll be back for sure

M W.

Yelp

I purchased tickets to see Ja Rule and Ashanti after Lovers and Friends was canceled. The website advertised that the concert started at 10:30 p.m. The actual purchased tickets stated that doors opened at 10:30. My wife and I stayed until a little after 1:00 a.m. and neither Ashanti nor Ja Rule had made an appearance yet. We had to leave because we had only booked a babysitter to a certain time. I looked on Instagram and found out they did not perform until about 2:30 a.m. There were no announcements that indicated it would take that long for the performance to start. It is ridiculous that it would take 4 hours for a performance that was advertised as starting at 10:30 to start. I would be very careful booking concert tickets here. The only reason I'm not giving it 1 star is because the venue is gorgeous and the music was fantastic. Also, this is a small vene and it was absolutely packed when we left and there were a massive amount of people waiting to get inside.

![Image 90: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/cjEtI1xm400EwYfj7YBDMw/180s.jpg)

Brenda A.

Yelp

Awful. Had us waiting in line for two + hours to only come and find out that we weren't even going to get in. Staff is extremely rude and unprofessional. Broke my toe because people kept stepping over me, thank you.

![Image 91: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/GL0W1vS7iAbM3XaoC1tK4g/180s.jpg)

Alexandrina B.

Yelp

I saw Akon at LIV and it was the best time ever! I love the venue and lights! It's like a mini Omnia. I would definitely go to see it!

![Image 92: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/1tQxN-4VsRaJOdMVjtNkBQ/180s.jpg)

Melissa B.

Yelp

The bouncers / door supervisors were extremely rude from the start. They came off as aggressive and annoyed. They had no intentions to serve their clients or customers. I don't plan on coming back, or recommending this nightclub to anyone in my network.

![Image 93: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/HlvS2BG0j_8-6q7zhuRGJw/180s.jpg)

Sleep F.

Yelp

Took a friend from France here since we've been to Miami location. Host wearing Jordans w/a suit walked by and told my friend to "Watch his mouth" for no reason, maybe he heard something different. Accents. However, such initial disrespect is enough to easily avoid taking any of our other international friends there. Bar tenders & Security do their job well. Great Sound!

![Image 94: google avatar](https://s3-media0.fl.yelpcdn.com/photo/tyHkiCvAQ-u8atgmH9o0gA/180s.jpg)

Victoria G.

Yelp

Worst night club in the strip! It was so ridiculous how long you had to wait to get in even if you got there at a decent time. I wasn't in the mood to wait (I was on a guest list ) so I asked if I could pay they were rude and said no then later closer to the artist coming out they said we had to pay even more to get in even tho we were already checked in from the guest list and practically at the door already. They've been open for almost six months at this point and they still over book EVEN IF YOU ARE VIP their line was worse

Greg G.

Yelp

My group pre-purchased $150 dollar tickets to see John Summit on Saturday night 5/25/24. we showed our tickets and were granted access to the club level on top of the escalators but when we arrived to the actual club entrance the scene was completely chaotic and unorganized. We were told the event had been oversold and we would have to wait until people in the club had left before entering. There were probably 300 other people waiting at the entrance. Staff was rude and unhelpful when we asked about why we couldn't get in even with pre purchased tickets. We waited for an hour and the line didn't budge. It was a big act on a Saturday night so the people in the show were not likely to leave until the show was over. Rude staff, bad vibe, greedy promoters and just an overall disrespect for paying customers. compared to the clubs in Vegas the whole set up was amateur hour. There are many better nightlife options in Vegas don't waste your time and money at LIV.

Margarito S.

Yelp

From Miami to Chicago I've been working with Brian Pfeiffer 773-459-8133 for several years now he always comes through with the best tables that are very reasonable and less than online price. Whether heading to Miami or Chicago or Las Vegas make sure you hit them up he'll hook you up.

Raquel O.

Yelp

This was the worst club I have ever been to in my entire life. We were on the guest list and even arrived early, only for them to make us wait 4 HOURS and still make us pay. Every single one of the promoters who are running this show are dismissive, entitled, and extremely rude. Especially FRANK, PATRICK, AND DAVID. Extremely overpacked. Everyone is so crammed into such a small space, like if we were sardines. Out of every single club out in Vegas, this is by far the most unorganized and overpriced one. Believe me when I say, save yourself the aggravation, time, and money with this club.

**Liv Nightclub: Vegas new and Hottest Club!**

Exciting news from the heart of Las Vegas's vibrant nightlife scene

**What is Liv Nightclub?**

I'd like to share some exciting news from the heart of Las Vegas's vibrant nightlife scene. The Fontainebleau Las Vegas, an epitome of luxury and entertainment, is gearing up for its grand launch on December 13, 2023. Following this much-anticipated opening, LIV Las Vegas, a premium nightlife venue within the resort, created by the renowned Groot Hospitality under David Grutman, is set to make its debut on December 14. This grand opening will be marked by the inaugural residency of John Summit, a luminary in the electronic music sphere.

Need Liv Nightclub reservations? [Book Now](https://myvegasbookings.com/)

![Image 1: Nightclub illuminated with blue light features multiple levels, a crowd of people, and an eye-catching lighting display on the ceiling](https://optim.tildacdn.net/tild6630-3061-4232-b232-663366363939/-/resize/780x/-/format/webp/Picture1.jpg.webp)

David Grutman, the visionary behind LIV, expressed his enthusiasm for Summit's residency, emphasizing LIV's legacy in hosting top-tier talent. LIV Las Vegas is poised to continue this tradition, setting a new benchmark in the city's nightlife.

![Image 2: Complete blackness](https://thb.tildacdn.net/tild6337-6634-4431-b638-656265323262/-/empty/Picture1.jpg)

John Summit, originally from Chicago and now a Miami influencer, has made his mark on major music festivals like EDC Las Vegas and Creamfields North. As the founder of Experts Only, his influence extends beyond performances to shaping the electronic music industry. Summit's residency at LIV Las Vegas is a pivotal moment in his career, offering a new dimension to his global tour schedule which includes stops in Germany, Australia, and major U.S. cities.

Summit himself is thrilled about this opportunity, acknowledging Groot Hospitality's iconic status in the industry and expressing his eagerness to bring a fresh vibe to Fontainebleau Las Vegas.

Komodo 

The design of LIV Las Vegas, crafted by the award-winning David Rockwell and Rockwell Group, is a masterpiece in itself. Spanning 50,000 square feet, the venue is engineered to provide an intimate yet high-energy atmosphere, ensuring that every guest has an exceptional view of the stage. This thoughtful design has positioned LIV as a leading venue since its original inception in Miami Beach in 2008, contributing to David Grutman's recognition as a key influencer in the EDM world. 

Papi Steak 

Three other iconic Miami Beach venues are also coming to the desert: , Papi Steak, and Komodo, as well as the LIV Beach Dayclub, a new addition to the portfolio, opening in 2024. Rockwell Group designed all Groot-operated spaces in the resort, which opens in December after 16 years in development and construction. The immersive, extravagant interiors for each venue reflect the overarching design concept of the hotel, carrying all the excitement and glamour of the original @Fontainebleau to the Las Vega Strip. 

Liv Beach Club 

Guests staying at Fontainebleau Las Vegas will enjoy expedited access to LIV and Liv Beach Club Reservations can be made [here](https://myvegasbookings.com/) , and tickets for John Summit's premiere performance are available online.

In summary, LIV Las Vegas represents the pinnacle of nightlife luxury and entertainment, a cornerstone of 

the Fontainebleau Las Vegas experience. This new venue is a testament to the Fontainebleau brand's commitment to excellence and innovation in hospitality.

Fontainebleau Announces David Guetta Residency
==============================================

David Guetta sets his sights on Miami and Las Vegas in 2025 for a two-year DJ residency.

By [Isabel Rivera](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/author/isabel-rivera/)June 18, 2024

![Image 4: Portrait of David Guetta](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/ww-media/mediaserver/mia/2024-25/photo-david-guetta-c2020-dan-reid.webp)

Grammy Award-winning DJ and producer David Guetta begins his two-year residency at the Fontainebleau Miami Beach and Fontainebleau Las Vegas in 2025.Photo by Dan Reid

Share this:

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.miaminewtimes.com%2Fmusic%2Fdavid-guetta-fontainebleau-miami-beach-las-vegas-residency-20351622%2F&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.miaminewtimes.com%2Fmusic%2Fdavid-guetta-fontainebleau-miami-beach-las-vegas-residency-20351622%2F&app_id=2962160854067219)

[](https://x.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.miaminewtimes.com%2Fmusic%2Fdavid-guetta-fontainebleau-miami-beach-las-vegas-residency-20351622%2F&text=Fontainebleau%20Announces%20David%20Guetta%20Residency&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.miaminewtimes.com%2Fmusic%2Fdavid-guetta-fontainebleau-miami-beach-las-vegas-residency-20351622%2F)

[](mailto:?subject=Fontainebleau%20Announces%20David%20Guetta%20Residency&body=Fontainebleau%20Announces%20David%20Guetta%20Residency%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.miaminewtimes.com%2Fmusic%2Fdavid-guetta-fontainebleau-miami-beach-las-vegas-residency-20351622%2F)

![Image 5: Carbonatix Pre-Player Loader](https://gamalpha.com/images/tts-pre-loader.gif)Audio By Carbonatix

EDM’s favorite Frenchman is coming your way, Miami.

Beginning in 2025, DJ-producer extraordinaire [David Guetta](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/things-to-do-at-home-david-guetta-covid-19-fundraiser-dj-set-from-miami-11622341) is set to start an exclusive two-year residency at the Fontainebleau Miami Beach’s [LIV nightclub](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/location/liv-6422397) and its newest counterpart, the Fontainebleau Las Vegas’ LIV Beach.

The collaboration comes as little surprise considering Guetta’s history with the Magic City – the star has established himself as a regular headliner at Ultra Music Festival and bought a waterfront mansion on Billionaire’s Bunker just last year – and LIV owner David Grutman’s notoriety for his high-profile collaborations with celebrities the likes of Pharrell Williams and Bad Bunny.

In a statement, Fontainebleau’s chief executive officer Jeffrey Soffer lauded the DJ’s class and charisma as exemplary of the hotel’s brand, calling him a “natural fit for the luxury lifestyle and vibrant energy of LIV and LIV Beach.” If Guetta’s billion-stream amassing club classics like “I’m Good (Blue),” “Sexy Bitch,” “Titanium,” and “When Love Takes Over” are any indication, the DJ’s residency sets are sure to deliver a promising soundtrack to the Magic City’s hedonistic hotspot.

### Editor's Picks

*   [David Guetta Invites the World to Tune In to His Live DJ Set From Downtown Miami](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/things-to-do-at-home-david-guetta-covid-19-fundraiser-dj-set-from-miami-11622341/)
*   [David Guetta Moves to Edgewater: “This Is a Little More Cool, a Little More Cultural”](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/opinion/david-guetta-moves-to-edgewater-this-is-a-little-more-cool-a-little-more-cultural-6473954/)
*   [David Guetta Talks Art Basel, Pop Success, and the Rift Between WMC and Ultra](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/music/david-guetta-talks-art-basel-pop-success-and-the-rift-between-wmc-and-ultra-6438173/)

The announcement follows the start of Guetta’s current Future Rave 2024 residency at HÁ¯ Ibiza, ranked as the best nightclub in the world by _DJ Mag_, on June 7 alongside Danish DJ Morten. The shows, which take place on Fridays from June through October, are packed to the brim and feature mind-bending light shows coupled with acclaimed guest artists from across the globe, including Abel, Danny Tenaglia, Mark Kight, Tchami, and more.

Though Guetta’s roots in the electronic music genre stem as far back as 1984, the DJ first achieved mainstream success with “When Love Takes Over,” a breakthrough single off of his fourth studio album, _One Love_, that has since ranked as [the number one dance-pop collaboration ever](https://www.billboard.com/lists/top-dance-pop-collaborations/david-guetta-and-kelly-rowland-when-love-takes-over-2009/). He followed this feat up with chart-topping albums like _Nothing But the Beat_ and collaborations with pop industry giants Sia, Nicki Minaj, and Rihanna, even coining a new EDM subgenre, future rave, in 2019. The musical style, which is a combination of techno and progressive house marked by its rolling grooves and aggressive synths, has become the official sound of his Ibizan residency of the same name and is likely what LIV attendees can expect to hear.

While Guetta has had a years-long affair with the 305, his burgeoning relationship with Sin City looks bright despite largely being contained to the annual EDC Las Vegas Festival until now. Considering LIV Beach’s poolside paradise claim as a “one-of-a-kind enclave for fun in the sun” reminiscent of the French Riviera, Guetta is sure to feel as if he’s never left the coast, excitedly sharing, “I get excited every time I’m about to perform at LIV in Miami, and now I cannot wait to start a fresh chapter at LIV Las Vegas inside the Strip’s newest luxury resort. It is going to be incredible!”

For assistance, the Box Office can be reached Monday through Friday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM via email at [\[email protected\]](https://www.fontainebleaulasvegas.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#75171a0d1a13131c161035131719140603101214065b161a18) or by calling [702-678-9780.](tel:+17026789780) During the week, the Concierge Desk is available for in-person Box Office assistance and ticket sales.

Is re-entry allowed?Most events will allow re-entry for ticketholders. Entry is cutoff to all guests approximately 15 minutes prior to a show’s scheduled end time.

What is the bag policy?Backpacks, bags, or purses may not exceed 8.5 inches by 11 inches in size. All bags are subject to search by Security prior to entry.  
  
_For all items not allowed in the BleauLive Theater, please see [full disclaimer here](https://www.fontainebleaulasvegas.com/terms/bleaulive-theater-disclaimer/)._

What is the camera policy?Video camcorders, professional cameras, detachable lenses,tripods, selfie sticks, audio recording devices, and/or tablets are not permitted. Select events may prohibit all photography and require guests to lock up their devices prior to entry.  
  
_For all items not allowed in the BleauLive Theater, please see [full disclaimer here](https://www.fontainebleaulasvegas.com/terms/bleaulive-theater-disclaimer/)._

What is the smoking policy?Smoking and vaping is not permitted inside the Theater. Guests are permitted to smoke tobacco products on the Casino floor only.

Can I use cash to buy tickets, drinks, or merchandise?BleauLive Theater is a cashless venue. No cash is accepted at points of purchase.

Is outside food and drink allowed?Outside food is not permitted. Beverages must be transferred to a provided plastic cup prior to entry.

Is food and drink available for purchase?Bars offering a full-bar selection of beverages and an array of concessions are available on all levels of the theater.

What accessible or ADA accommodations are available?Accessible seating options for wheelchair and wheelchair-transfer seating are generally available for purchase via Ticketmaster.com, subject to availability. Wheelchair spaces and sight/hearing impaired accommodations can be requested by contacting the Box Office at [\[email protected\]](https://www.fontainebleaulasvegas.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#64060b1c0b02020d070124020608051712010305174a070b09). Sign interpreters can requested from the Box Office with no less than four-weeks-notice to show date. Guests who require accessible entry may use the Priority Entry line or request special entry from a Theater security officer upon arrival.

Do I receive Fontainebleau Rewards Bleau Points for ticket purchases? Can I redeem Bleau Points for show tickets?Bleau Points cannot be earned or redeemed for ticket purchases at this time.

##### They have similar names and they both serve the masses — but for two decidedly different reasons. Learn more about the LIV Miami nightclub’s trademark dispute with Saudi-backed LIV Golf.

The LIV Miami nightclub has a bone to pick with [LIV Golf](https://boardroom.tv/tag/liv-golf/). The popular beachside [party venue](https://www.livnightclub.com/) at the iconic Fontainebleau Hotel recently filed a court action to oppose the Saudi-funded league’s attempt to register a series of trademarks regarding its chosen name.

You may file this under “things I didn’t expect to see today,” but such is the predicament of plenty of upstart business trying to secure various logos and marks that make up their identities.

Poetically enough, LIV Golf counts the Trump National Doral Miami in the nearby city of Doral as one of its competition venues.

Per trademark attorney Josh Gerben of [Gerben Intellectual Property](https://www.gerbenlaw.com/), LIV nightclub owner David Grutman filed the Notice of Opposition. Since opening its doors in 2008 at the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel, the spot is beloved by Miami residents and celebrities alike. Because it can also hosts live performances, its become a popular spot for musicians to take the stage in front of thousands of fans.

In the document, Grutman claims LIV Golf’s trademarks are “confusingly similar” to those of the Miami venue. The businessman argues the marks are “visually, phonetically, and aurally similar and the goods/services share similarities,” consequently, the public may mistakenly believe the [golf](http://boardroom.tv/tag/golf) competition is connected with or endorsed by LIV nightclub.

[GolfWeek](https://golfweek.usatoday.com/2023/03/15/liv-golf-news-legal-battle-liv-nightclub/) and others have noted that both brands decided on “LIV” based on the Roman numerals representing 54 — LIV Golf events are 54 holes rather than the typical 72, with 54 additionally being considered a type of hypothetical perfect score (100% birdies) on a par-72 course. Meanwhile, the LIV Miami nightclub site was first established in 1954 and has been at times referred to as “Miami’s Studio 54,” a nod to the defunct but legendary Manhattan venue.

Founed in 2021, LIV Golf is backed by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign Public Investment Fund, with two-time Open Championship winner Greg Norman serving as CEO. Due to [the nature of its backing](https://boardroom.tv/public-investment-fund-sovereign-immunity-liv-golf/) and its aggressive [recruitment](https://boardroom.tv/abraham-ancer-liv-golf/) of [PGA Tour](http://boardroom.tv/tag/pga-toru) players, the league has found itself entrenched in controversy in the court of public opinion as well as various courts of law.

At press time, the US Patent and Trademark Office website lists the case as still “pending.” Stay tuned for more legal fireworks.
